findings.problem: Job struct uses `status: String` (primitive) instead of a domain enum or typestate. Any string value including "foo", "", or invalid transitions like "completed" -> "running" are representable.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid job states can be constructed at compile time; no runtime enforcement of valid status transitions; business logic must repeat string-equality checks everywhere
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a domain enum `JobStatus { Pending, Running, Completed, Failed }` (or similar) and use it as the sole status carrier

findings.problem: Job struct uses two independent lifecycle booleans `started: bool, completed: bool`. These allow impossible combinations: both false with status "running", both true, completed without started, started after completed.
findings.failure_mode: The compiler cannot enforce that lifecycle is monotonic or that exactly one lifecycle stage holds; invalid combinations silently pass construction and only surface as bugs at runtime
findings.fix: Replace `started: bool, completed: bool` with a single typestate enum `Lifecycle { NotStarted, Started, Completed }` that makes illegal combinations unrepresentable

findings.problem: `Job::new()` is an infallible constructor that accepts raw primitives and stores them directly with zero validation. It can construct a Job where status="running" but lifecycle booleans are false, or status="".
findings.failure_mode: Every call to `new()` can produce a logically invalid Job; all callers inherit the invalid state and must defensively check, or silently operate on corrupt data
findings.fix: Replace `new()` with a fallible smart constructor or derive-into from validated inputs. Use `From`/`Into` for the newtype enum so construction goes through the enum constructors which are exhaustive by construction

findings.problem: `update_status(&mut self, new_status: &str)` accepts any string and assigns it unconditionally. No state-machine transition check (e.g., cannot transition from Completed back to Running).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state transitions are silently accepted (e.g., Completed -> Running), corrupting the job lifecycle; downstream logic relying on monotonic lifecycle will behave incorrectly
findings.fix: Replace with a typed method such as `fn transition_to(&mut self, target: JobStatus)` that enforces valid transitions via an enum match or transition table

findings.problem: `get_status(&self) -> &str` leaks the internal `String` type as a raw `&str`. Combined with the primitive `String` status, this exposes implementation details and offers no type safety at call sites.
findings.failure_mode: Callers receive a naked `&str` and must compare against string literals instead of matching on enum variants, making them brittle to renaming and unable to exhaustively handle all states
findings.fix: Return `&JobStatus` (or `JobStatus` if Copy) so callers match on the domain enum rather than comparing strings

findings.problem: `created_at: Option<String>` and `completed_at: Option<String>` use raw `String` for timestamps. No type safety, no parsing guarantees, no canonical format enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Timestamps can hold any invalid string ("not-a-date", "", random text); no compile-time or constructor-time guarantee of valid timestamp format; downstream consumers must re-parse and re-validate everywhere
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `Timestamp` (or use a crate like `chrono::DateTime`) and store `Option<Timestamp>` instead of `Option<String>`; validate at the parse boundary

findings.problem: The entire Job struct is mutable imperative state with no functional core. `update_status` mutates in place; there is no pure transition function that takes a Job and returns a new Job or a Result.
findings.failure_mode: State mutations are side-effectful and irreversible; no ability to reason about state transitions declaratively; harder to test, harder to replay, harder to reason about correctness
findings.fix: Add a pure transition function `fn transition(job: &Job, target: JobStatus) -> Result<Job, TransitionError>` in the functional core; keep the mutable struct only at the imperative shell boundary

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for any performance claims. The crate has zero benchmark targets.
findings.failure_mode: Any stated performance characteristics are unsubstantiated; no evidence that changes do not regress
findings.fix: Add `[[bench]]` section in Cargo.toml with criterion or similar, and benchmark the hot path (transition logic, status checks)

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, cadvisor) exists for the code path.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation hotspots and CPU-bound paths are unknown; optimizations are cargo-culted rather than evidence-driven
findings.fix: Run `cargo flamegraph` or `perf record` on representative workloads to identify actual hotspots before optimizing

findings.problem: No verification commands (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy) have been executed or evidenced.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm the codebase compiles cleanly under the Holzman strict-gate lints
findings.fix: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test`; record exact commands and outputs in the review ledger

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler/benchmark data to substantiate allocation or throughput claims
no cargo test / cargo clippy / cargo fmt command evidence
no second-ring command evidence (e.g., Miri, Kani) for state transitions
residual_risk: The Job type is a primitive-anemic struct with no typestate enforcement, no constructor validation, and no state-machine transitions. Invalid states are fully representable and constructible at compile time. Without replacing `String`/`bool` fields with enums/typestates and adding a fallible smart constructor, any consumer of this API operates on potentially corrupt state. Static review only; no commands run.
